clue.text: Rank and file in shop cheer start of strike

parts.note: to shop someone is British slang for informing on them, as is to grass
to root for a team is to cheer it on

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of strike is used

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Ordinary union members gather in a shop to cheer as a strike begins.
explanation.definitionFit: The grass roots of a party or movement are its ordinary members, the rank and file as opposed to leaders.

clue.text: Travelling with no one, one gets whacked before dinner

indicators.note: the travelling word must have no one in it, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: going somewhere is travelling
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lone traveller is told off and punished at a meal stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner gong is struck to summon a household to the meal, so it is the thing hit before dinner.

clue.text: Old-fashioned restaurant I queued to get in

indicators.note: the answer gets in among these words, sitting inside them across the word breaks

parts.note: the answer runs from the end of restaurant through I into queued

explanation.surface: Someone recalls having to stand in line to get into a quaint restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something antique is old and of a former era, so it can describe anything old-fashioned.

clue.text: Do hands help for people struggling?

parts.note: a do is a party or social gathering, a social
farm or factory hands are workers

explanation.surface: A question asking whether hired labourers assist people having a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like the start of a question but it is the noun for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Social workers are professionals employed to support vulnerable people and families in difficulty.

clue.text: Telly Savalas's opening do, surprisingly square

indicators.note: the letters end up in a surprising new order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the opening of a name is its first letter

parts.note: the surname whose first letter is taken
taken as written

explanation.surface: The bald actor Telly Savalas throws a launch party that turns out to be oddly conventional.
explanation.definitionFit: Square is slang for conventional and unfashionable, which is what old-style means.

clue.text: European waterway on part that's elevated

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces are raised, so they read from the bottom up

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a memo
a bit is a part of something

explanation.surface: A canal or river in Europe sits on a raised section of land.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiber is the river flowing through Rome in Italy.

clue.text: Alibi's abandoned by Capone — this may haunt the banks

indicators.note: the gangster's first name leaves the word, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A gangster ditches his excuses, and something comes back to trouble the banks he robbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haunt the banks' suggests a robbery; the banks are riverbanks, which a wading bird frequents.
explanation.definitionFit: An ibis is a long-billed wading bird that frequents river banks and marshes.

clue.text: Mastermind should include it here?

indicators.note: the word for mastermind takes it in, holding it inside

parts.note: a mastermind is a brain behind a plan
taken as written

explanation.surface: A query about whether the TV quiz Mastermind ought to feature something in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: Mastermind is a long-running BBC quiz show; here it is just a clever planner.
explanation.definitionFit: For a British newspaper's solver, here means the country it is published in.

clue.text: Worthwhile novel fits in proverb

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the proverb word

parts.note: a proverb is a saying

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A worthwhile new book contains a well-known proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A satisfying task gives fulfilment, which is what makes something feel worthwhile.

clue.text: Observed, beginning of last month, weight returned

indicators.note: the whole sequence comes back the other way, reading right to left

parts.note: December is the last month, abbreviated DEC
the first, or day one, of the month, written as the numeral I
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone saw that at the start of December their weight had come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning of last month' reads as 1 December, DEC I, before the weight follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To have noticed something is to have seen or observed it.

clue.text: Parisian who tucks into veg in silence

indicators.note: the French word goes inside the vegetable

parts.note: beet, or beetroot, is a vegetable
qui is French for who

explanation.surface: A Parisian eats vegetables without saying a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucks into' suggests eating, but it means going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Silence! as a command is the same order as telling someone to hush.

clue.text: Weakened after fast, becoming irritable

indicators.note: the weakened word comes after the fast word

parts.note: quick means fast
to temper is to moderate or soften

explanation.surface: Someone grows weak and cranky after a period of not eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like a period without food; it is simply speedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick-tempered person is easily angered, which is being irritable.

clue.text: Competition round examinations board's first

indicators.note: the board word comes first, ahead of the examinations

parts.note: to board is to lodge, also to quarter, and 's here is is
finals are final-year university examinations

explanation.surface: An exam board takes the lead in a contest's round of examinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' suggests an exam board, but it is the verb meaning to house someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The quarter-finals are the stage of a knockout tournament before the semi-finals.

clue.text: Where spirits are taken out without exorcism?

definitions.text: Where spirits are taken out without exorcism?

parts.note: spirits read as ghosts, removed from a place; really strong drinks bought to take home
suggests no priest is needed; the shop holds a licence to sell alcohol for drinking off the premises

explanation.surface: A place where ghosts are removed without any religious rite.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is the name for a shop licensed to sell alcohol to be consumed elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A British liquor store sells drink, spirits included, under a licence for consumption off the premises.

clue.text: Liberty offers complimentary Shakespeare, abridged?

parts.note: complimentary tickets are free

indicators.note: the first name is cut short, losing its tail

parts.note: William Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A theatre's offer of free tickets to a shortened Shakespeare play.
explanation.definitionFit: Free will is the liberty to choose one's own actions.

clue.text: TV company rings hotel, needing to eat

indicators.note: the TV company surrounds the hotel word like a ring

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster
an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: A broadcaster phones a hotel because it wants a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings' suggests a phone call; it means encircles.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinny person is very thin, someone who looks as if they need feeding up.

clue.text: Tango, except around Spain, may be short on melody

indicators.note: the word for except goes around Spain's letter

parts.note: unless can mean except
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A tango played anywhere but Spain might lack a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuneless music lacks melody, being short of any recognisable air.

clue.text: Large flightless bird's catching rook and other creatures

indicators.note: the bird's letters catch the rook inside them

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless bird, and 's adds S

explanation.surface: A big ostrich-like bird snatches a rook along with other animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are primates of Madagascar, animals other than the birds in the surface.

clue.text: Sign showing motorists parking within 20-minute walk?

indicators.note: the motorists park inside the walking distance

parts.note: a mile takes about twenty minutes to walk
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A road sign tells drivers there is parking a short walk away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' suggests a road sign; it is a sign in the biblical sense of a wonder.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospels a miracle is called a sign, an act showing divine power.

clue.text: Flipped over American with hair treatment, an incredibly powerful figure

indicators.note: the word for American is turned over, reading backwards

parts.note: a perm is a hairdressing treatment
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American goes wild about a hairdo that gives an amazing look.
explanation.definitionFit: Superman is the comic-book hero of superhuman strength.

clue.text: Middle-of-the-road companies looking to North and South African territory

parts.note: MOR is the radio abbreviation for middle-of-the-road music

indicators.note: the pair of companies reads the same up or down the column

parts.note: two CO abbreviations for company, one turned round

explanation.surface: Mainstream firms look in both directions for territory in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Morocco is a kingdom in north-west Africa.

clue.text: Rent-a-car pet's wee permeates internally — cleaner needed!

indicators.note: the answer lies inside these words, running across their breaks

parts.note: the answer runs from car through pet's and wee into permeates

explanation.surface: A dog's urine has soaked into a hire car, so someone must clean it.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpet sweeper is a hand-pushed device with rotating brushes for cleaning rugs.

clue.text: One's slowly progressing in moving home

definitions.text: One's slowly progressing in moving home

parts.note: a creature that is slow-moving
sounds like someone relocating house; it carries its shell, its home, with it

explanation.surface: Someone is making slow progress with a house move.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail is a slow mollusc that carries its shell, its home, on its back.

clue.text: Spill the beans, but a different vegetable's picked up

indicators.note: picked up as in heard, so the word is matched by its sound

parts.note: the leek is an onion-like vegetable, different from beans

explanation.surface: Someone drops the beans, but grabs a different vegetable instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To leak information is to reveal a secret, an idiom for spilling the beans.

clue.text: Casino's corruption embroils island city

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap round the island letter
the casino's letters are corrupted, twisted into a new order

parts.note: the word casino as written; the possessive just links it to corruption

explanation.surface: Crooked dealings at a casino drag an island into scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus.

clue.text: Repair fancy heel occasionally causing pain

indicators.note: only now and then a letter is used, every other one

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of these words

explanation.surface: Mending a fancy shoe's heel brings on aches.
explanation.definitionFit: Earache is a pain felt in the ear.

clue.text: First Lady appears by right on any occasion

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: The US President's wife shows up beside the right-wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means at any time, as in 'if ever', so on any occasion.

clue.text: Enigmatic individual, intimate with Democrat — arrest must follow

indicators.note: the arrest word comes after the rest

parts.note: close friends are intimate
police book someone when they arrest them

explanation.surface: A politician friendly with a Democrat is about to be arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed book is a person whose thoughts are hidden, someone hard to read.
